details:
TerraTwin is a web-based exploratory planetary analog atlas designed to investigate similarities between selected Earth environments and regions on the Moon and Mars.

Users can explore 12 selected Earth candidate sites and four lunar and Martian target regions, inspect available evidence, compare environmental features, and explore how mission-objective priorities affect provisional candidate rankings.

The platform organizes information across eight environmental dimensions: slope, surface roughness, temperature contrast, dryness, vegetation and bareness, rock and mineral type, water ice and permafrost, and dust and aerosol context. Its main components include an interactive map, site catalogue, comparison views, and mission scenario controls.

The project aims to support planetary analog research, environmental exploration, and communication of potential Earth analog locations. Earth environments cannot fully reproduce extraterrestrial conditions such as reduced gravity, vacuum, and radiation. Therefore, TerraTwin is an exploratory prototype rather than a validated landing-site selection or mission-suitability system. Missing evidence is kept unavailable instead of being treated as zero, and all scores and rankings are provisional.

The prototype uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Python-based data preparation, Leaflet, and OpenStreetMap.

AI Assistance Disclosure: Our team used the Antigravity AI Agent and ChatGPT for coding assistance, debugging, and documentation drafting. AI-assisted outputs were reviewed and tested by the team. Scientific data and provisional results are not treated as validated solely because of AI assistance.

Live Project: https://amarahan.github.io/TerraTwin/

Source Code: https://github.com/Amarahan/TerraTwin
